## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sirikāḷakaṇṇijātaka* (Ja 192), translated into English as "Lucky Unlucky," is a short entry in the Pali Jātaka collection. In the standard edition of the text, it appears in the second nipāta directly between the *Ruhakajātaka* (Ja 191) and the *Cullapadumajātaka* (Ja 193) [Fausböll 1879]. The entry does not preserve an independent narrative; rather, it records only the opening canonical verse lemma—*Itthi siyā rūpavatī ti* ("Even though women may be fair")—and provides an explicit cross-reference noting that the full story will be made evident in the *Mahā-ummagga Jātaka* (*Idaṁ Sirikāḷakaṇṇijātakaṁ Mahā-ummaggajātake āvibhavissatī ti*) [Fausböll 1879].

 Automated text-reuse computation by DharmaNexus identifies three internal Pali matches with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Chaṭṭho bhāgo, Atk S0514a2), sharing 384 characters with its longest alignment running from §0.4–2.4 to §2393–2398 [DharmaNexus]. This computational match directly mirrors the commentary's incorporation and explanation of the story within the later *Mahā-ummagga Jātaka* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches with a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus].
